Exact leave-one-out for species with high Pareto k

Source: R/loo_refit.R
loo_refit.Rd

PSIS-LOO approximates leaving a species out by reweighting the posterior draws of the full fit. For influential species (Pareto k above about 0.7) the approximation is unreliable. loo_refit() refits the model without each such species and replaces its contribution by the exact value log mean_s p(y_i | y_-i, theta_s), with theta_s drawn from the posterior given the other species.

Usage

loo_refit(fit, loo = NULL, k_threshold = 0.7, ...)

Arguments

fit

A Bayesian phylogp_fit.

loo

Optional result of loo(fit); computed if missing.

k_threshold

Species with Pareto k above this value are refitted.

...

Further arguments to $sample().

Value

The loo object with the pointwise and total estimates updated for the refitted species (their Pareto k set to 0, as in loo::reloo()), and an attribute refitted naming them.

Details

A species is left out by giving it a measurement-error standard deviation many times larger than the spread of the data, so its value carries no information while the tree, and any latent rates on it, stay the same. Its predictive density is then computed in linear time (branch-wise kernels) or by dense conditioning.
